narrative.overview: The application behaves like a teaching instrument built into a dark electronics bench. Code enters at the left bay, passes through a deliberate Run switch, and arrives as readable output at the right bay. The visible signal path makes the learning workflow—edit, run, read, ask—feel physical and repeatable without imitating a professional IDE.
keyCharacteristics: A visible horizontal signal bus connects editing, execution, and feedback.
Graphite instrument faces, recessed wells, steel edges, and warm printed labels.
Amber is reserved for live action and signal flow; green means ready or successful; red means a recoverable fault.
Compact corners, precise alignment, and tactile controls replace soft dashboard cards.

rules.name: The One Live Signal Rule
rules.body: Amber marks only the current action, focus, or moving signal. It never becomes ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Instrument Truth Rule
rules.body: Every light, line, scale, and label communicates real workflow or state.

rules.name: The Printed Legend Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracking belongs on concise equipment labels, never on paragraphs or decorative eyebrows.

rules.name: The Recess Before Float Rule
rules.body: Working areas are inset into their panels. Avoid floating translucent cards and colored halos.

dos: Do make edit → run → read visible in composition and state.
Do use instrument labels only for real controls, channels, and statuses.
Do keep stdout and stderr exact, readable, and easy to use in an AI prompt.
Do retain clear browser affordances and keyboard focus.
donts: Don't use glass panels, neon gradient fields, or generic AI dashboard cards.
Don't add decorative meters, graphs, lights, or technical markings without real meaning.
Don't compress guidance until a beginner cannot understand the next action.
Don't let visual character obscure Monaco, output, language selection, or Run Code.
